questions.question: Six letters S, T, M, P, R and C are written on different faces of a dice. Two positions of this dice are shown in the figures below. Find the letter on the face opposite to M.
questions.questionHtml: Six letters S, T, M, P, R and C are written on different faces of a dice. Two positions of this dice are shown in the figures below. Find the letter on the face opposite to M.
questions.solution:
As T is common on both the dices, it is clear that S, M, P, and R are adjacent to it, and the remaining i.e. C will be opposite to it.

​

Opposite pairs:

M → R

S → P

T → C

So, the opposite side of "M" will be side "R".

questions.question: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (7, 9, 48) (6, 8, 42) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.questionHtml:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set.
(7, 9, 48)
(6, 8, 42)
(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent
digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1
and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.solution:
Option 3) (11, 13, 72)

(11 + 13) × 3 = 72 

24 × 3 = 72

72 = 72 (LHS = RHS)

Thus, out of all the options, '(11, 13, 72)' follows the same logic as given.

(NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed).
questions.solution:
Option 3) 3 – 2 – 5

3 × 2 = 5

6 ≠ 5 (LHS ≠ RHS)

Thus, out of all the options, '3 – 2 – 5' is the odd one out.

questions.question: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some boxes are cartons. All cartons are papers. Some cartons are utensils. Conclusion (I): No box is a utensil. Conclusion (II): Some papers are utensils.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.
Statements: Some boxes are cartons. All cartons are papers. Some cartons are utensils.
Conclusion (I): No box is a utensil.
Conclusion (II): Some papers are utensils.
questions.solution:
Conclusions:

I. No box is a utensil → Does not follow (As some boxes are cartons, all cartons are papers and some cartons are utensils. As no direct relation is given between boxes and utensils, therefore it is false.)

II. Some papers are utensils → Follow (As all cartons are papers and some cartons are utensils. As whole cartons comes in papers and has some part common with utensils, therefore it is true.)

∴ Here, Only conclusion (II) follows.
